elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The inserted covenant reads only "shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000" - no commercial general liability limit appears anywhere; Paragraph 5.3 and the cost definition at p0133 are permissive/cost-allocation language with no coverage obligation.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: No aggregate CGL limit is stated in the inserted INSURANCE paragraph or elsewhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause sets E&O at "not less than USD 1,000,000", which is the fallback amount and below the preferred USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted cyber and privacy limit is "not less than USD 2,000,000", below the preferred USD 5,000,000; the clause also contains no data-processing trigger.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation covenant is inserted; Paragraph 25 (compliance with law) is a general compliance covenant, not an insurance obligation.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: The inserted paragraph contains no certificate-on-request mechanic.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative language: "Each Terminal Party and each Maintenance Authority shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000" - mandatory ("shall maintain"), bound on the counterparty-analogue operators identified in Paragraph 10.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence: "and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000" - express cyber/privacy line at the fallback limit.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: both fallback elements (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy USD 2,000,000) are carried by a single mandatory "shall maintain" covenant, not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred level remains incomplete - to reach it the drafter would need to add CGL of USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate, raise E&O to USD 2,000,000, raise cyber/privacy to USD 5,000,000 with a Customer Data processing trigger, add workers' compensation as required by law, and add certificates of insurance on request.

Minimality holds: for a missing clause a concise insertion may be wholly new wording, and the drafter correctly omitted the model clause's at-own-expense language and one-year survival tail, plus the preferred-only CGL, workers' compensation and certificate mechanics, none of which the selected fallback elements require. No existing words were deleted and no operative term is duplicated (Paragraph 5.3's voluntary self-insurance and the p0133 cost definition are left intact).

Intent preserved: the new covenant sits alongside, and does not contradict, Paragraph 5.3 (permissive own-cost insurance) or the Capital Costs treatment of jointly agreed insurance at p0133 - it adds a floor rather than displacing the cost-sharing mechanic; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is introduced, since "Terminal Party" and "Maintenance Authority" are existing Agreement roles referenced in Paragraph 10.

Drafting note (rationale-level, not a defect against the checklist): the insertion has no temporal anchor ("throughout the term"), so the duration of the obligation is inferred from the Agreement generally; also confirm our client is not itself a Terminal Party or Maintenance Authority, or the covenant will bind us as well as the operators.
